candidates.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
candidates.abstract: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sinδ$ dependence to be probed in $ν_μ$ survival probability. candidates.title: Observation of rotonic density enhancement at the boundary of a uniform dipolar superfluid
candidates.abstract: The collective excitations of a quantum liquid lie at the heart of its emergent behaviour. In many systems, the variation of excitation energy ${\varepsilon}$ with wavevector $k$ exhibits a softening at a characteristic lengthscale, which plays a key role in thermodynamics and transport. These excitations, termed rotons, often reflect an underlying tendency of the liquid to crystallize into a competing symmetry-broken state, such as the solid state of helium or the Wigner crystal of electrons in a magnetic field. More than $50$ years ago, it was predicted that rotons should manifest as emergent density oscillations at the fluid's boundary, but this effect has not been observed. Here, we realize an ultracold dipolar superfluid confined in a homogeneous trapping potential and directly confirm the emergence of rotonic density enhancement at its edge. This is accompanied by rotonic density fluctuations across the bulk, which are linked to the static edge structure via the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. candidates.title: Soft--hard Bayesian inference in heavy-ion collisions
candidates.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures. Contribution to the proceedings of Hard Probes 2026 (Nashville, Tennessee, 21-26 June 2026)
candidates.abstract: Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. candidates.title: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE -- II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
candidates.comment: 22 pages, 6 Figures, 6 Tables. Accepted in MNRAS
candidates.abstract: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500--5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators ($v\sin i$ $\leq$ 30 km~s$^{-1}$) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and $λ$~Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with \tona, and the \bacc\ code. We obtained median abundances of $ε$(C) = 8.37$\pm$0.10, $ε$(N) = 7.35$\pm$0.16, $ε$(O) = 8.63$\pm$0.08, $ε$(S) = 7.19$\pm$0.18, and $ε$(Fe) = 7.45$\pm$0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] $=-0.48$), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1--0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. candidates.title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models
candidates.abstract: Cardiovascular imaging offers several ways to measure blood flow, but each provides an incomplete, resolution-limited, or noisy view of the underlying dynamics. Reconstructing the missing information is inherently ambiguous because several flow fields may be compatible with the same observation. Here, we investigate generative diffusion models as tools for cardiovascular-flow generation and reconstruction using a fully controlled state-of-the-art dataset from a digital twin of a healthy human left heart. First, we show how unconditional samples reproduce the changing anatomy and the highly fluctuating statistical properties of the flow throughout the cardiac cycle. Second, we test the conditional inference of our generative model by reconstructing an entire 2D planar section of geometry and flow configurations from a limited portion. Repeated reconstructions allow us to represent a range of plausible completions, going beyond a single deterministic estimate, while their mean retains the principal features of the reference flow. candidates.title: Soft-photon resummation for low-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders
candidates.abstract: We present resummed predictions for $e^+e^- \to μ^+μ^-(γ)$ and $π^+π^-(γ)$ in the multi-photon soft limit, matched to exact NLO. The resummation is performed within the Yennie-Frautschi-Suura framework at the amplitude level. The initial and final-state contributions are included coherently, and NLO accuracy with finite electron, muon and pion masses is achieved. We present our calculation, its implementation in a fast Fortran Monte Carlo integrator, and compare our predictions with the generators BabaYaga, KKMC, Phokhara and McMule, in scenarios inspired by the energy-scan (CMD) and radiative-return (KLOE, BES III, B factories) experiments. We find agreement with BabaYaga, which includes higher-order corrections through a parton shower, at the per-mille level in the cross-sections, and differences of up to two percent with the soft-photon resummation of KKMC. This work represents an important step towards the validation of Monte Carlo generators for low-energy experiments, and will be released in the upcoming new version of Phokhara.

candidates.title: Network versus market information in coupled opinion-return dynamics
candidates.abstract: When making investment decisions, investors can use common signals from the market and local signals from their social networks. We develop an agent-based opinion-return model in which agents follow fixed trading strategies and respond to either local network information or a common market signal. In our model, trend followers and contrarians select either a local network signal or a common market signal and then update their buy, hold, or sell opinions by following or opposing the signal, respectively. The aggregate opinion imbalance determines the return, which sets the market signal. We find that three collective regimes emerge depending on how much network information is used and the fraction of contrarians in the population. Persistent directional states occur when trend followers dominate, market-wide reversals appear when a contrarian-rich population relies on the common market signal, and opposing opinions coexist with small aggregate returns when the same population relies on network signals. candidates.title: Feasibility study of two-stage direct laser acceleration of electrons
candidates.abstract: We present the first numerical demonstration of two-stage direct laser acceleration (DLA) of electrons. The result was obtained using quasi-3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. The first stage ($a_0 = 6$, $τ= 200~\mathrm{fs}$, $w = 4λ$, $λ= 0.8~μ\mathrm{m}$) utilized a nitrogen gas target with an atomic density of $n_a = 0.008n_{cr}$. This stage was designed to accelerate low-energy electrons, achieving a maximum energy of approximately 94 MeV with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 7.0$ MeV and $T_2 = 16.0$ MeV) and a charge of 6.04 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). The resulting electron bunch was then injected into the second stage, where hydrogen at a lower density ($n_a = 0.01n_{cr}$) was used, while the laser parameters were the same as in the first stage except that the waist was increased to $w = 8λ$. After the second stage, the electrons reached energies up to 225 MeV, with a two-temperature energy spectrum ($T_1 = 18.4$ MeV and $T_2 = 88.3$ MeV) and a charge of 4.55 nC ($\mathcal{E} > 5$ MeV). candidates.title: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
candidates.abstract: Simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the Galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWB). Realistic features such as non-Gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (SBI) to augment traditional analyses. Here, we present an SBI framework for LISA stochastic component separation built on the Simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. We progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law SGWB. candidates.title: Pseudo-entropy in Thouless Pumps and Majorana Topological Phases
candidates.abstract: We study the average excess pseudo entropy, $ΔS_{12}$, in the Rice-Mele model under Thouless pumping. We compute it for two driving schemes, the control-freak and smooth pumps, under open and periodic boundary conditions. We find that $ΔS_{12}$ distinguishes the trivial, monomer, and topological stages of the pump, and that it depends on the boundary condition, the driving scheme, and the reference time. We also find that a nonzero staggered potential breaks chiral symmetry and gaps out the SSH critical point, thereby flattening the pseudo-entropy peak at the phase boundary. We also study reference-state dependence in the open Kitaev chain, comparing a fixed even-parity target with five reference families: even free-fermion, pairing-only, vacuum, and two fixed gapped states. We find that the pseudo-entropy response depends on the reference and on the parity of the subsystem size, even when the reference remains gapped. At $μ=0$, the pairing-only reference gives the exact result $S_{\mathrm{pr}}=\ln 2$ for $L=4m+2$, while the $L=4m$ sequence has analytically determined finite-size corrections. candidates.title: Heat cleaning kinetics and thermal degradation of MOCVD-grown GaAs photocathodes
candidates.abstract: We evaluated metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaAs/GaAsP strained-superlattice photocathodes with integrated distributed Bragg reflectors in a low-voltage Mott polarimeter at Jefferson Lab. Without a protective arsenic cap, surface contamination can develop during transport and installation. Heat cleaning removes this contamination by thermally desorbing material bound to the surface, but excessive heating can also damage the photocathode. We modeled quantum efficiency (QE) in terms of surface contaminant coverage to describe its increase with heating time. QE rose more rapidly and reached a plateau nearly twice as high at $550^\circ\text{C}$ as at $450^\circ\text{C}$, while polarization remained near 83%. Further heating reduced QE and polarization. Reflectance measurements showed a shift of the optical resonance to shorter wavelengths, consistent with surface material loss. We also tested the cleaning method in a high-voltage photogun, where QE showed the same initial increase and subsequent decline. The cleaning procedure must therefore balance contaminant removal against loss of photocathode material.

candidates.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
candidates.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, contribution to the Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea
candidates.abstract: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.

candidates.title: What determines the properties of Population III binaries?
candidates.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures. Abstract abridged for arxiv
candidates.abstract: Population~III binaries may provide a gravitational-wave probe of the first stellar populations. Uncertain initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions complicate predictions of their remnant masses, birth orbits and formation spins. Varying these model evolutionary parameters (MEPs) jointly is needed to identify which MEPs shape each property and whether their effects persist among binaries that merge. We use \textsc{StarTrack} to evolve $2\times10^6$ initial binaries per model across 1152 configurations spanning eight MEPs. To our knowledge, this is the largest grid of Population~III isolated-binary population-synthesis models to date by number of distinct parameter configurations. We compare the properties and correlations of all binary black holes (BBHs) with those of systems that merge within the adopted age of the Universe. The all-BBH (merging-BBH) model medians span $34.3$--$171.0 M_{\odot}$ ($23.1$--$94.8 M_{\odot}$) in total mass, $0.039$--$0.106$ ($0.018$--$0.129$) in effective aligned spin $χ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ at formation, and $0.075$--$0.639$ ($0.039$--$0.983$) in birth eccentricity. candidates.title: Balancing heavy flavour: Quantum number compensation in the hadronisation of charm and beauty particles in proton-proton collisions
candidates.abstract: The hadronisation of heavy quarks remains one of the least understood processes of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). While the production of heavy quark pairs can be calculated perturbatively in QCD, the subsequent formation of hadrons involves non-perturbative processes. The description of these processes is predominantly model dependent and sensitive to the underlying mechanisms of colour reconnection and string fragmentation. In particular, the conservation of flavour, baryon number and charge imposes constraints on how heavy-flavour hadrons are formed and balanced within the final state. In this work, we study how the quantum numbers associated with charm and beauty production are balanced in proton-proton collisions, using events simulated with the PYTHIA-8 event generator. Starting from perturbatively produced ($c\overline{c}$) and ($b\overline{b}$) pairs, we examine how the formation of heavy-flavour mesons and baryons, including $D^0$, $B^+$, $Λ_c^+$, and $Λ_b^0$, is accompanied by compensating particles elsewhere. candidates.abstract: Out-of-plane polarization can be tuned by sliding polar monolayers in van der Waals materials; the bulk photovoltaic effect is emerging as a natural optical probe, provided the photocurrent tracks the polarization. We test that assumption by computing the polarization and the shift-current tensor from first principles across the stacking landscape of bi-, tri-, and tetralayer hexagonal boron nitride. The two quantities share one robust property: the vertical response reverses with the polarization while the in-plane one does not. candidates.title: Single-Pulse Dosimetry for Ultra-High-Dose-Rate X-Ray Pulses Based on Radiation-Induced Acoustic Signals
candidates.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement. 17 pages, 4 figures
candidates.abstract: Real-time dosimetry of ultra-high-dose-rate (UHDR) pulsed X-rays remains a major challenge. This proof-of-principle study investigates a dosimetry method for UHDR pulsed X-rays based on radiation-induced acoustic (RA) signals from a thin metal foil. The foil combines efficient X-ray absorption and acoustic resonance, converting deposited dose into acoustic signals with discrete resonant frequencies. Single-pulse measurements were performed at six dose levels spanning approximately 1--40 mGy(Si), with one pulse recorded at each level and instantaneous dose rates reaching the order of 10^6 Gy/s at the highest dose settings. The peak-to-peak amplified transducer-output voltage exhibited a linear relationship with the reference dose measured by thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLDs). These results demonstrate the feasibility of single-pulse acoustic dosimetry under the tested conditions. Furthermore, we establish analytical solutions for radiation-induced acoustic signals in a one-dimensional layered medium in both the time and frequency domains, providing a theoretical basis for signal interpretation and detector optimization.

candidates.title: Quantum conditional relative entropy and quasi-factorization
candidates.comment: Submitted as chapter for the book "Entropy, Relative Entropy, and Quantum Information Theory"
candidates.abstract: One of the characteristic features that distinguishes quantum systems from classical ones is the inability, except for some special cases, of defining a conditional expectation map for a given quantum state, namely a map that restricts observables to a given sub-region (or more generally, a sub-algebra of observables) while preserving expectation values. candidates.comment: 18 pages, 19 figures, 4 tables. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

candidates.abstract: Massive black holes (MBHs) are found in galactic centres, but their formation and evolution remain elusive. candidates.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, preprint submitted to Elsevier
candidates.abstract: Hyperbolic metamaterials (HMMs) made of alternating layers of metal and dielectric have been heralded as promising materials for super-resolution imaging and spontaneous emission enhancement sought after in biological applications. However, the practical utilization of HMMs has been limited, primarily by the solid and stiff nature of the underlying substrate, usually a silicon wafer or glass substrate. candidates.abstract: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.

candidates.abstract: Pulsations and binarity are important properties of massive stars and influence their structure and evolution. Young open clusters are ideal laboratories to study massive stars, since they are mostly coeval and chemically homogeneous. We analyse 82 B-type stars in the Galactic open clusters $h$ and $χ$ Persei, NGC 457, NGC 581, and NGC 1960, which have ages between 15 and 30 Myr. We extract light curves using both simple aperture photometry and a point-spread-function-based method that minimises contamination from crowded fields in full-frame images from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. We successfully extract light curves for 63 stars. The majority have photometric variability caused by pulsations, showing how pulsations are a common property of young B-type stars in clusters. We classify stars into different pulsator types based on their spectral type and frequency spectrum. candidates.comment: Article accepted for pubblication by RASTI with official acceptance date 20/11/2026
candidates.abstract: High-precision photometric missions are sensitive to flux contamination from neighboring stars, which can bias light curves, dilute transit depths, and compromise photometric precision. We present PHOTO-CAT, a catalog-driven, mission-agnostic tool for quantifying stellar flux contamination in photometric observations. The tool builds a three-dimensional Euclidean representation of the sky from a user-provided astrometric catalog, indexes it with a memory-optimized KDTree for rapid neighbor searches, and computes per-target contamination metrics from angular separation, relative fluxes, and configurable aperture models (top-hat or circular Gaussian PSF), optionally converted into an arbitrary instrumental bandpass via empirical photometric relations or stellar spectral models. A streaming, CSR-style storage format with compact internal identifiers enables scalable processing of catalogs with tens to hundreds of millions of sources with minimal memory overhead. Outputs include per-target contaminating flux, contamination ratios, target purity, number of neighboring sources, and their angular separations, supporting target screening and field-selection decisions ahead of observations.

candidates.abstract: Suppressing vortex shedding behind a circular cylinder is a classical problem in active flow control.Model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) learns such policies by interacting with the flow without differentiating its dynamics, which typically requires a large interaction budget. This study optimises closed-loop policies by differentiable simulation: control-loss gradients propagate through the simulated flow to the policy parameters, which are updated by reverse-mode automatic differentiation. The policy maps local velocity measurements to a jet amplitude imposed through differentiable synthetic-jet boundary conditions. In a two-dimensional confined cylinder wake at Rey=100, eight policy updates (about 78 shedding periods of forward simulation) give approximately 8% drag reduction and 99.6% suppression of lift fluctuations, the drag level being comparable to reported DRL results. Suppression is sustained by feedback: a mean-matched constant jet does not maintain it, whereas the same policy responds similarly at three activation phases and recovers after upstream disturbances. A velocity-deviation reward alone retains strong suppression, and observations of two instantaneous

candidates.title: Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones
candidates.abstract: We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. We start by establishing a no-go result proving that no reasonable genuine multipartite entanglement entropy can simultaneously obey LOCC-monotonicity and subadditivity. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.

candidates.title: Coronagraphic time-delay interferometry: fundamental steps towards concrete applications
candidates.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatory. Central to LISA data analysis is time-delay interferometry (TDI), which reduces otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. In previous work, we explored coronagraphic TDI, a sky-dependent null-stream channel which cancels the GW signal of a point-like source when pointed at its sky position. Because this property relies only on the geometric response of LISA, coronagraphic TDI is a candidate for model-agnostic sky localization. Here, we address three challenges which arise when analyzing realistic LISA data: (i) spacecraft motion; (ii) signal superposition; (iii) instrumental noise. We derive a second-generation coronagraphic TDI variable and its analytic noise model, and show that it reduces laser frequency noise in the presence of spacecraft motion while still recovering the position of the source. Using pairs of Galactic binaries (GBs), we find that sources can be localized independently provided they do not overlap in frequency, even when they share the same sky position, whereas sources overlapping in frequency can only be localized if one dominates by a factor of ~100

candidates.title: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
candidates.comment: 36 pages, 4 figures, 'Online resource 1' included at the end of the paper
candidates.abstract: Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose

candidates.title: Chromatic calorimetry using nanocomposites: status and future challenges
candidates.comment: Contribution to the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026)
candidates.abstract: The development of advanced detector technologies will play a key role in future high-energy physics experiments, such as the FCC-ee. In this context, chromatic calorimetry is an emerging concept for electromagnetic calorimeters, with the potential to combine the precise energy measurement of homogeneous calorimeters with longitudinal reconstruction of particle showers. The state of the art in chromatic calorimetry is reviewed, including experimental results from proof-of-concept prototypes and simulation studies investigating quantum-dot-based configurations. Recent progress and current challenges in the development of nanocomposites are also discussed. Finally, future prospects for chromatic calorimetry are outlined.

candidates.title: Navigating Quantum Education at the University level: Pedagogical Pathways and a Roadmap for Textbook Selection
candidates.abstract: Instruction in quantum mechanics (QM) is often categorized by its entry point as 'wave-first' or 'spin-first', yet these labels lack consistent definitions and overlook other established or emerging approaches. Moreover, while capturing broad differences in topic selection and sequencing, this binary framing obscures critical differences in contextualization--how three dimensions (mathematical tools, phenomena and experiments, and theoretical concepts) are framed and connected to support student sensemaking. Research also rarely examines how such pedagogical choices unfold across the undergraduate-to-graduate trajectory. Using textbooks as an analytical lens to map these choices and characterize overarching pathways, encompassing entry points and overall orientations, we comparatively analyze the selection, sequencing, and contextualization of core topics across these 3 dimensions, alongside prefaces and introductions, in 36 university QM textbooks spanning countries and eras. At the topic level, we show that identical topics occupy widely different curricular roles depending on their contextualization. Synthesizing these findings into pathways, we identify three additional entry-p

candidates.title: Nuclear Urca cooling in magnetar crust and anomalous heating
candidates.abstract: We present a new result that the nuclear Urca process in magnetars, associated with ultrastrong magnetic field, dramatically alters the neutrino cooling efficiency to support higher surface temper ature, which is not common in ordinary neutron stars. A new formalism for neutrino luminosity accommodating finite temperature on top of magnetic field is extended with the use of realistic nuclear structure inputs for the Urca pair 29Na-29Mg. We find that the neutrino luminosity of Urca pair shows a spiral variation as a function of magnetic field and crust density, while the Urca pair persists, in contrast to previous studies. Applying geometrically correct volumetric energy loss rate to Urca shell at fixed density with varying magnetic field strength, our results show that thermally populated excited states at finite temperature enhance neutrino luminosity, whereas conditions con strained Urca-pair formation driven by ultrastrong magnetic field reduce cooling efficiency, which can explain high temperature of magnetar surface as a new possibility.

candidates.title: Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
candidates.abstract: We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.

candidates.title: Geometrical Estimation of Electromagnetic Degrees of Freedom in Reflecting Environments
candidates.abstract: The number of spatial degrees of freedom (NDoF) of electromagnetic communication channels in reflecting environments is investigated using a full-vector formulation based on dyadic Green's functions and equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents. The channel correlation eigenproblem characterizes the electromagnetic communication modes and their coupling strengths, while the leading-order NDoF is estimated geometrically from the receiver-accessible phase space volume in the electrically large regime. By combining two geometrical projection Jacobians, the phase space volume is related to the mutual shadow area, establishing the equivalence between the two geometrical NDoF formulations and yielding a two-polarization estimate equal to twice the mutual shadow area divided by the squared wavelength. The free-space mutual shadow formulation is extended to perfect electric conductor (PEC) reflecting environments through image construction and phase space ray tracing, accounting for specular reflections and geometrical visibility constraints. The formulation is validated against the eigenvalue spectra of full-vector electromagnetic channels involving planar PEC reflectors, a parabo

candidates.title: Quantum-Informed Regularized Poisson Learning for Graph-Based Semi-Supervised Classification
candidates.abstract: We introduce IPQSSL, a quantum-informed regularized Poisson framework for graph-based semi-supervised classification under scarce labels. Local graph feature contexts are QR factorized, lifted to unitary encodings, and processed by a shared variational circuit whose measurements yield node wise diagonal weights that stabilize a symmetrized Poisson system. We establish positive definiteness of the symmetrized, regularized operator under explicit spectral conditions and derive a Hermitian, block encoding compatible formulation that separates the classical NISQ oriented implementation from a future fault-tolerant pathway. Across seven benchmarks spanning tabular data and a citation network, the effect of regularization is dataset- and budget-dependent: IPQSSL improves over the Poisson baselines on Iris and Wine at all but the single-label budget, reaching 0.946 accuracy on Iris at ten labels per class and at every budget on German Credit, where, however, all methods remain below the majority class rate. Original Poisson remains preferable on Breast Cancer, Heart Disease, Optdigits, and Cora, with the deficit narrowing as the label budget grows on the two largest graphs. Ablations attr

candidates.title: Effective theory of quantum black holes with Kretschmann scalar
candidates.comment: 12 pages, 15 figures, under review in European Physical Journal C
candidates.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamics, quasinormal modes (QNMs), and shadows of the effective theory of quantum black holes (BHs) by expanding the physical constants in terms of the Kretschmann scalar. The resulting effective metric can contain two horizons, which is typical for a quantum-corrected Schwarzschild spacetime. The second-order corrected metric only shifts the first-order corrected metric, allowing investigation of IR phenomena from the pure first-order corrected one. From a thermodynamic point of view, the metric leads to a stable cold remnant with zero entropy, compatible with the third law of thermodynamics. In the perturbation regime, we use massless scalar perturbations to extract the effective potential, QNMs, graybody factor, and total absorption cross section. We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $Ω/χ^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section are

candidates.title: Forbidden T-symmetry breaking in time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with gain and loss
candidates.abstract: Parity-time ($PT$) symmetry has attracted significant interest in photonics and related fields in recent years. With sufficiently weak gain and loss, these systems typically exhibit entirely real energy levels, with all corresponding wave functions remaining $PT$ symmetric. As the strength of gain and loss increases, complex-conjugate energy levels are expected to emerge, signaling the onset of $PT$ symmetry breaking. Similar properties can be found in non-Hermitian systems with other antilinear symmetries as well, where parity is replaced by another operator such as rotation ($R$) or simply the identity operator, resulting in $RT$-symmetric and $T$-symmetric non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we demonstrate that this typical scenario of non-Hermitian symmetry breaking in a finite Hilbert space is forbidden in a class of time-dependent systems with gain and loss and $T$ symmetry: the system remains in its $T$-symmetric phase as we increase the strength of gain and loss, even when the spatial distribution of gain and loss is random. Furthermore, this behavior is also independent of the duration or period of the temporal modulation. In contrast, this forbidden non-Hermitian symmetr

candidates.title: Atomic interferometry based on a phase-jump error signal with suppression of the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift
candidates.abstract: We develop a method for forming Ramsey fringes in atomic interferometers as a difference error signal using the phase-jump technique for Ramsey pulses (phase-jump error signal). In this case, the measurement procedure can be implemented as stabilization (locking) of the frequency chirp rate at the central zero of the error signal. We show analytically that this approach allows suppressing the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift (LACS). This shift was recently theoretically predicted and experimentally identified in the papers [V. I. Yudin et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{122}, 737 (2025); D. N. Kapusta et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{123}, 388 (2026)]. A characteristic feature of the LACS is an inverse cubic dependence $\propto 1/T^3$ (where $T$ is the time between adjacent Ramsey pulses), and it can become dominant for interferometers with a short baseline. Therefore, the developed measurement algorithm with a phase-jump error signal will enable significant improvement in the metrological performance of compact quantum sensors for various purposes (atomic gravimeters, accelerometers, gyroscopes).

candidates.title: Test of gravitational redshift by optical clocks at different latitudes
candidates.abstract: General relativity predicts that frequency comparisons between clocks are affected by both gravitational and kinematic time dilation. While the kinematic contribution has been tested with high accuracy, experimental tests of the gravitational redshift remain comparatively less stringent. Here, we measure the frequency shift between two Earth-fixed optical atomic clocks at different potentials and compare it to the redshift predicted by general relativity using independent geodetic measurements. The observed shift agrees with the prediction, testing the gravitational redshift at the $4.6 \times 10^{-5}$ uncertainty level, improving ground-based tests by a factor two. Previous ground-based tests separated the clocks mainly vertically. For clocks at different latitudes, their height difference is governed not only by the gravitational potentials at their locations but also by the centrifugal potentials caused by Earth's rotation. As both contributions can partially cancel, the gravitational contribution can be considerably larger than their height difference suggests. In this work, a separation of the clocks by $4^\circ$ in latitude enhances their sensitivity to a gravitational redshi

candidates.title: Block Search Conditioned on Features for Sequential Quantum Data Encoding
candidates.comment: 6 pages, 1 figure. Prepared for ESANN 2027. Code and reproduction scripts: https://github.com/CeciliaBotelho/ESANN-2026
candidates.abstract: Sequential quantum data encoding is addressed through the joint selection of input features and encoding blocks within a fixed quantum register. At each step, a new feature, a block of operations, its placement, and its rotation weights are selected together from training data, extending the incremental construction of Q-FLAIR. With direct-loss selection (RAW), nine to twelve features were retained in four qubits across five new Bars and Stripes datasets. Under the same final calibration, mean changes relative to the calibrated Q-FLAIR reference were +5.53 percentage points in balanced accuracy, -15.83% in binary cross-entropy (BCE), and +7.79% in area under the ROC curve (AUC). The prespecified success criterion was met in four of five datasets and for the mean paired differences. These results were obtained by comparing complete procedures under a common cap of 32 operations.

candidates.title: Edge-dislocation interactions with sub 3 nm vacancy and interstitial clusters in FeCr alloys: Mechanisms, Obstacle strength and Fate
candidates.comment: 23 pages, 9 figures, supplementary material included. Submitted to Journal of Nuclear Materials
candidates.abstract: Fe-Cr alloys harden at irradiation doses where transmission electron microscopy (TEM) shows no defects, implicating defects too small to be resolved. Their obstacle strength is unknown, so hardening models ignore them and fit measured hardening to visible defects alone. Here, molecular dynamics drives an edge dislocation through relaxed 1-3 nm vacancy and mixed Fe-Cr interstitial clusters in Fe-3Cr, Fe-5Cr and Fe-10Cr at 300 K. Vacancy clusters relax into platelets whose strength rises with size to about 350 MPa at 2.9 nm, following strong-obstacle scaling independently of Cr content, and always survive dislocation passage. Interstitial clusters relax into $\frac{1}{2}\langle 111 \rangle$, mixed or $\langle 100 \rangle$ loops. They are mostly weaker than platelets of the same size, their strength varies up to fivefold with the local Cr arrangement, and most are absorbed. Only $\langle 100 \rangle$ loops in Fe-5Cr and Fe-10Cr often survive. During pinning, Cr collects at the junction between these loops and the dislocation; atom tracking for one loop shows that more than half comes from the loop itself. candidates.title: Lacrymaria-like dynamics: compression and length change in active slender bodies
candidates.abstract: Length change is central to the behaviour of many active slender bodies, yet most elastohydrodynamic models of microscopic locomotion treat filaments as effectively inextensible. Here we introduce a compressible $N$-link formulation for planar active filaments, in which both bending angles and segment lengths are dynamical variables coupled through local hydrodynamic drag, modelled using resistive force theory. We first use the model to test whether passive extensibility can improve bending-driven swimming and crawling. Across the parameter ranges studied, passive compressibility usually reduces locomotion speed, indicating that axial compliance alone is not a robust mechanism for propulsion enhancement. We then prescribe active rest-length waves and show that compression can either enhance, suppress, or redirect locomotion depending on its phase, wavelength, and frequency relative to bending. Finally, motivated by the extensible neck dynamics of \textit{Lacrymaria olor}, we apply the method to clamped and free filaments driven by oscillatory follower forces. candidates.title: The Kerr Metric in Canonical Harmonic Coordinates to All Orders
candidates.comment: 36 pages. Codes available at Github https://github.com/pierrevanhove/kerr-metric-harmonic and Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/24397114
candidates.abstract: We give in closed form the transformation from Boyer--Lindquist coordinates to the canonical harmonic coordinates of the Kerr metric, to all orders in Newton's constant and in the spin. This is the canonical harmonic chart selected by the MPM prescription and by the harmonic-gauge Einstein recursion sourced by the Kerr multipoles, with the residual homogeneous freedom fixed by the boundary conditions. The chart is the real, time-reversal-covariant combination of the two radial harmonic functions underlying the Cook--Scheel coordinates, which differ from it by a definite residual harmonic transformation. The proof rests on a classification of the residual harmonic freedom. Rotational covariance, parity, time reversal and analyticity in the spin allow a decaying homogeneous solution beyond the linear field only in the spatial components at third post-Minkowskian order, with angular degree $\ell=p+2$ at spin order $a^p$. This sector is a pure gauge mode, equivalent to an MPM gauge moment. candidates.title: A sliding mode observer perspective on chaos synchronisation of turbulent flows
candidates.abstract: State estimation of turbulent flows is challenging as infinitesimal prediction errors grow exponentially due to chaos. However, when signals from one chaotic system (the master) are injected into an identical system with different initial conditions (the slave), the slave can synchronise with the master --- a phenomenon observed in turbulent flows. From a control-theoretic perspective, this synchronisation problem can be viewed as observer design. We first show that synchronisation by direct substitution of observed variables into the slave system is equivalent to a sliding mode observer. This perspective enables the analytical verification of stability as well as the design of feedback for robustness. We focus on reduced-order Navier--Stokes models with quadratic non-linearities, a broad class of systems for which stability can be analysed by seeking Lyapunov functions through parameter-dependent linear matrix inequalities solved via semidefinite programming. candidates.title: Banana D-modules
candidates.abstract: We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. Two properties of the banana $D$-module are studied: its holonomic rank and the irreducibility of the monodromy representation. This is achieved by relating the banana $D$-module to Lauricella $F_{C}$ hypergeometric systems. Further, we expand the generic-mass banana Feynman integral and the associated discontinuity integral in terms of series solutions. Finally, we analyze the Pfaffian system arising from the banana $D$-module and construct an explicit $d\log$ representation in the equal-mass specialization.

candidates.title: geodesiq: a Python package for geometric diabatic-adiabatic optimal state transfer
candidates.abstract: We introduce the geodesiq Python package, which implements a geometric framework for shaping control pulses that achieve high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel quantum systems. The underlying method combines adiabatic and diabatic control into a single metric, suppressing unwanted excitations while allowing selected diabatic passages. Finding the pulse thereby reduces to solving a single first-order ordinary differential equation. We explain how to use geodesiq and illustrate its use explicitly with Landau-Zener transitions, spin-qubit initialization, adiabatic many-body ground-state preparation, and a diabatic-adiabatic transfer in a four-level system.

candidates.title: Nutrient limitation drives Turing instabilities in cross-feeding microbial communities
candidates.abstract: Microbial communities are shaped by metabolic interactions, often in the form of cross-feeding in which microbes exchange metabolites via diffusion through the environment. We show here that the diffusion of cross-fed metabolites generically leads to a Turing instability in resource-poor environments, driven by the feedback between local metabolite availability and cell growth. A coarse-grained model of community biomass identifies the few dimensionless parameters that control the instability, most notably the ratio of environmental energy supply to cellular maintenance costs. We find that the detailed topology of the metabolic interaction network can be coarse-grained into a single effective parameter to quantitatively characterise the instability. Beyond the onset of the instability, the community forms compact aggregates whose merger is prevented by a competition for shared resources. Overall, our results demonstrate how spatial structure can arise as an inevitable consequence of metabolic interactions in a microbial community.

candidates.title: Actively stabilized Fabry-Pérot notch filters for correlated photons from cold two-level atoms
candidates.abstract: We report two actively stabilized Fabry-Pérot cavities operated as reflection-mode notch filters for biphotons generated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a cold two-level atomic ensemble. In this source, elastic scattering at the excitation frequency increases the single-detector count rates and the accidental-coincidence background, thereby limiting the observed nonclassical correlations. One cavity is placed in each photon-collection mode. An acousto-optic modulator frequency-dithers an auxiliary field, and synchronous demodulation of the transmitted power provides the locking discriminator. Light resonant with the auxiliary field is transmitted, whereas the detuned components are reflected toward the photon detectors. By tuning the auxiliary field to the same frequency as the excitation field, we filter these components and direct a larger portion of the quantum-correlated sidebands to the detection. The cavities have linewidths of approximately 2 MHz and remain locked for longer than a typical correlation acquisition. candidates.title: Hard X-ray spectroscopy of a short-period asynchronous polar: IGR J19552+0044
candidates.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ
candidates.abstract: IGR J19552+0044 is an asynchronous polar with a beat modulation of $\approx2$ days due to $\approx3$% spin-orbit asynchronism. We present the first hard X-ray properties of this system using a NuSTAR observation. Spectral modeling yields a shock temperature of $kT_{\rm s}=44.50^{+3.60}_{-3.29}$ keV, implying a white dwarf mass of $M_{\rm WD}\geq 0.85\,M_\odot$. We infer an average accretion rate of $\dot{M}\sim 3.0\times 10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, consistent with expectations for short-period systems (orbital period $<2$ h). Even at this low accretion rate, we detect a significant Compton reflection component that gives a shock height of $H\sim 0.3\,R_{\rm WD}$. Time-resolved spectroscopy of the observation, covering $\approx61$% of a beat cycle, reveals a variation in $\dot{M}$ by a factor of $\sim 4.5$, providing X-ray evidence for the magnetic valve mechanism. Despite the large variations in $\dot{M}$, no significant change in shock temperature is observed. This weak thermal response constrains the shock structure on the white dwarf surface, favoring a shock height that remains approximately constant as $\dot{M}$ changes, potentially due to variations in the fractional a

candidates.title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
candidates.abstract: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS fluxes. Deriving the BMS charges requires additional care, since BMS generators extended into the bulk are generally not tangent to the null hypersurfaces. After accounting for this and the associated anomalies, the renormalized canonical charges still contain an additional soft contribution. The prescription of a covariant boundary Lagrangian determines a corner improvement that removes this term and recovers the standard BMS charges.

candidates.title: Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning
candidates.abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models are often limited by exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input variations as system size increases. In this work, we provide a comparative empirical study of this phenomenon across Fidelity Quantum Kernels (FQK), Projected Quantum Kernels (PQK), and Quantum Extreme Learning (QEL), within a unified observable-based framework based on expectation-value variance. We investigate how measurement locality, entanglement, and circuit expressivity shape concentration across different architectures. Global fidelity-based kernels exhibit strong concentration driven by Hilbert space dimensionality, whereas local-observable approaches reduce but do not eliminate this effect. In PQK and QEL, concentration is primarily governed by entanglement and quantum dynamical expressivity, with reservoir depth emerging as a key factor in QEL architectures. We further study bandwidth scaling as a general mechanism for controlling encoding expressivity across all models. Our results indicate that bandwidth scaling effectively reduces concentration in moderate regimes by restricting the effective expressivity of the encoding, though t

candidates.title: Adaptive obstacle deposition drives dynamical localization in chase-and-escape dynamics
candidates.abstract: Most pursuit--evasion models assume a fixed environment, although defensive actions can leave persistent structures that affect subsequent encounters. We study a two-dimensional lattice model in which threatened escapers deposit permanent obstacles, coupling capture kinetics to the geometry explored by their pursuers. Increasing the deposition probability enhances escaper survival and strongly suppresses chaser transport. For dilute chasers, the mean-squared-displacement exponent decreases from values near unity towards zero, trajectories contract to a few lattice spacings and the localized fraction rises sharply. The localization response becomes weaker as chaser abundance increases. Time-resolved obstacle densities support a kinetic explanation: rapid capture depletes obstacle-producing escapers before a comparably confining environment can develop. At intermediate parameters, broad or bimodal distributions of trajectory radii and MSD exponents reveal simultaneous mobile and localized subpopulations. Thus deposition redistributes trajectories between distinct dynamical behaviors, producing heterogeneity beyond a uniform slowdown. We summarize the coupled survival and transport re

candidates.title: Diameter Growth of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ under Cliff Metrics
candidates.abstract: Cliff metrics are right invariant Riemannian metrics on the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ introduced by Nielsen and his collaborators in the geometric approach for gate complexity in quantum computations. In this paper, we compute the exponential growth rate for the diameter of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ equipped with cliff metrics as $N \rightarrow \infty$. We prove that if the norm of most generalized Pauli matrices are sufficiently large, this growth rate coincides with the growth rate of maximal gate complexity obtained by Knill.

candidates.title: The inverted harmonic oscillator in Segal-Bargmann space: Time-asymmetric propagator reconstruction and bi-coherent states
candidates.abstract: We investigate the real-time dynamics and resonance quantization of the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Its self-adjoint Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ has a real continuous spectrum, while generalized resonance states outside $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ have purely imaginary energies $\pm i\hbarω(n+1/2)$. In coordinate space, these states are expressed in terms of complex Hermite polynomials and are biorthonormal under the Fresnel Gaussian pairing. Adapting Moriconi's coordinate-time transformation to the real-time path integral, we derive the exact Feynman propagator. Using Mehler's formula, we show that each discrete expansion alone reconstructs the full unitary kernel on its time half-axis, with the decaying Gamow-Siegert branch converging for $T>0$ and the growing antiresonant branch converging for $T<0$. In the complex-scaled Segal-Bargmann representation, the two Hamiltonians take the form $\pm i\hbarω(z(d/dz)+1/2)$, and their monomial eigenfunctions map back to the dual complex Hermite states. candidates.title: Emergent Fourfold Symmetry in Polarization Images: Local Origin and Diffractive Breakdown
candidates.comment: Preprint. 8 pages, 3 figures. Supplementary material: 45 pages, 19 figures
candidates.abstract: A polarization image can gain or lose rotational symmetry with no change in material symmetry. In axisymmetric anisotropic systems, covariance restricts the field to azimuthal orders $m=0,\pm2$, guaranteeing twofold but not fourfold symmetry; pointwise unitarity adds fourfold symmetry, which diffraction can destroy. Holographic Jones fields of liquid-crystal torons show propagation shifts the twofold--fourfold balance; for the same director, a marching-wave model qualitatively reproduces the twofold morphology missed by a local model. This establishes a symmetry hierarchy for polarization imaging.

candidates.title: A Relativistic Newton's Third Law for Binaries in Environments
candidates.abstract: We derive the relativistic form of Newton's Third Law governing the interaction between intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and surrounding relativistic matter fields. Working within a two-parameter expansion, we rewrite the evolution of the secondary's orbital elements in a form resembling the integrated forces acting on the environment, avoiding the need to calculate any gravitational perturbations sourced by the dynamical matter content. Using the retarded and advanced Green's functions, we obtain both instantaneous and orbit-averaged laws relating the rate of change of the secondary's orbital energy and angular momentum to that of the matter and the gravitational-wave fluxes at that order. Our results clarify and correct the mixture of ad hoc balance prescriptions currently employed in the literature, providing first-principles forcing functions for the secondary's orbital elements in two ready-to-use forms: a leading-order formulation suitable for fast evaluation with complex relativistic matter simulations, and a first-post-adiabatic formulation of the energy and angular-momentum evolution in environments that are stationary and axisymmetric at leading order.

candidates.title: Decoupling Exciton Energetics from Wavefunction Geometry in Imide-Based Defect Double Antiperovskites
candidates.abstract: The excited-state properties of imide-based defect double antiperovskites AE$_5$AsPn(NH)$_2$ (AE = Ca, Sr; Pn = Sb, Bi) are investigated using spin--orbit-coupled quasiparticle calculations, the model Bethe--Salpeter equation (mBSE), and analytical descriptions of lattice-polarization effects. Across five tetragonal ($P4/mmm$) and monoclinic ($Cm$) structural models, the calculated exciton binding energies range from 140 to 210 meV. Chemical substitution modifies both the binding energies and the hydrogenic estimates of exciton spatial extent. By contrast, the structural distortion from tetragonal $P4/mmm$ ($D_{4h}$) to monoclinic $Cm$ ($C_s$), which removes inversion and fourfold rotational symmetry, produces comparatively modest changes in binding energy but appreciably reshapes the real- and momentum-space exciton distributions. This contrast reveals a partial decoupling between exciton energetics and wavefunction geometry, and identifies a symmetry-associated sensitivity of exciton geometry to structural distortion. The changes are understood to occur together with modifications of local coordination and electronic dispersion, rather than as an isolated effect of symmetry alone

candidates.title: Reset Quantum Channels
candidates.abstract: We introduce Reset Quantum Channels (RQCs), a class of quantum channels acting on a Hilbert space structured as a direct sum of an arbitrary number of subspaces. Within each subspace, the state evolves unitarily; across subspaces, it is transferred by measure-and-prepare resets along given states. In this general setting, we show that the determination of their invariant states reduces to a stochastic eigenvalue problem, whose size is set by the number of reset states rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space, and we discuss the uniqueness of these states. We further address the primitivity and the spectrum of these channels, which we compute explicitly when the reset states commute with the unitary evolutions. Applications include a small system coupled to several thermal reservoirs. We also consider random unitary evolutions and analyze the averages of the invariant states in this setup. Finally, we show that a suitable continuous-time limit yields Lindblad generators of reset type on the algebra of block-diagonal operators.

candidates.title: Structure-preserving compression of Matrix Product States
candidates.abstract: Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schrödinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.

candidates.title: How many states does an exact relaxation model need? Sharp state complexity and geometric obstructions for reversible chains
candidates.comment: 48 pages, 9 figures. Ancillary files contain exact certificates for 381 polygon-rate instances and verification scripts
candidates.abstract: How many states does a reversible Markov model need to reproduce two prescribed relaxation modes exactly? We maximize the smaller of the two stationary coordinate variances over all finite reversible chains whose states lie in a given convex region and whose coordinates relax at rates $1$ and $ρ$. Detailed balance turns this into the equilibrium of a tension-only cable network whose loads depend on the stationary masses. For the moment curve of the Wright-Fisher diffusion no finite chain is optimal: maximizing sequences converge to a unique beta law, and the best deficit with $N$ states is of order $N^{-2}$. We find the exact leading constant for states on the curve and for states in its convex hull, together with the optimal cube-root density of states. The hull constant is the curve constant times $c/(1+c)$, $c=(ρ-2)/ρ$; at $ρ=5/2$ the hull needs $\sqrt{6}$ times fewer states, although the limiting law is the same. For $ρ>8/3$ any upward enlargement of the hull lowers the constant again. All lower bounds hold for arbitrary transition graphs. At every fixed number of states an optimizer exists. candidates.title: Pure Orbitronics: Hall Responses and Torques by Orbital Exchange in Spinless Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides
candidates.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures. Submitted on 2 September 2026. Supplementary material available upon request
candidates.abstract: Recent studies have identified orbital exchange fields as a novel mechanism for controlling electronic and magnetic phenomena through the orbital degree of freedom. In contrast to conventional spin exchange fields, orbital exchange fields couple directly to orbital angular momentum and can emerge from purely orbital interactions or dynamically through couplings to chiral excitations such as phonons and magnons. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the transport and torque responses generated by orbital exchange fields in two-dimensional materials. Using monolayer H-phase MoS$_2$ as a prototypical transition-metal dichalcogenide, we introduce a Zeeman-like orbital exchange field that breaks time-reversal symmetry in orbital space while leaving the spin degree of freedom inactive. We demonstrate that this perturbation induces a sizable intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity even in the absence of spin magnetism and spin--orbit coupling driven mechanisms. Simultaneously, the orbital Hall response remains robust in the weak-field regime and undergoes substantial reconstruction at larger exchange strengths due to pronounced band modifications. candidates.title: Optimizing MHz X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy with burst-mode free-electron laser operation
candidates.abstract: Burst-mode X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide a powerful platform for X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) experiments with sub-microsecond temporal resolution, but the achievable performance is constrained in practice by both photon statistics and the sample's dose tolerance. Here, we develop an analytical framework for estimating the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of pulsed XPCS measurements, including pulse-to-pulse fluctuations of the incident intensity. We combine this description with dose constraints and show that, for a fixed maximum dose, acquiring fewer frames at higher per-pulse intensity yields a higher SNR than distributing the dose over a larger number of low-intensity frames. The framework is validated against measurements at the European XFEL, where the intensity fluctuations of the investigated operation mode are found to cause only a negligible reduction in SNR. We further introduce and experimentally demonstrate a rolling bunch pattern with three pulses per train and variable pulse spacings. candidates.title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
candidates.abstract: Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance. Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. candidates.title: Monolithic ultraviolet-to- near infrared photodetection enabled by an aluminium oxide photonic platform
candidates.abstract: Broadband photonic integrated circuits require waveguide platforms that combine low optical loss across a wide spectral range with integrated photodetection. Here we demonstrate a monolithically integrated atomic-layer-deposited (ALD) aluminium oxide (Al$_2$O$_3$)-on-silicon platform enabling waveguide-coupled photodetection from the ultraviolet to the near-infrared. The architecture employs evanescent coupling between low-loss Al$_2$O$_3$ waveguides and silicon p-i-n photodiodes. The platform supports photodetection at 375, 658 and 780 nm, extending integrated silicon photodetection into the ultraviolet. The devices exhibit linear photocurrent scaling with optical power, dark currents of approximately 2 pA at 50 V reverse bias and nanosecond-scale temporal response. We further demonstrate centimetre-scale ultraviolet Mach-Zehnder interferometer circuits with integrated photodiodes. The same detector architecture is implemented with Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguides, whereas the lower ultraviolet propagation loss of Al$_2$O$_3$ enables an approximately 15-fold higher photodetection response at 375 nm. These results establish ALD Al$_2$O$_3$ as a broadband integrated photonics platform for sen

candidates.title: Thermal photon production in massless boost-invariant gases: hydrodynamization without thermalization
candidates.abstract: We study hydrodynamization and thermalization in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions using relativistic kinetic theory. Modelling the quark-gluon plasma as a classical gas of massless particles undergoing a boost-invariant longitudinal expansion, we solve the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation via a semi-analytical method based on the method of moments. We show that the energy-momentum tensor is well described by relativistic fluid dynamics even when the system is far from local equilibrium. The single-particle distribution function, on the other hand, is not well approximated by a hydrodynamic truncation, suggesting that the onset of hydrodynamic behaviour does not require thermalization. We then quantify how the departure from equilibrium affects the emission rate of thermal photons in the forward scattering approximation, and show that non-equilibrium corrections beyond the hydrodynamic limit can have a significant impact on this observable.

candidates.title: Gap-label bounds and optical reconstruction of Landau-subband quantum geometry
candidates.abstract: We derive a magnetic gap-label lower bound on the internal quantum weight of Landau subbands that remains nonzero even when the occupied Chern number vanishes. Using the second fundamental forms of nested subbundles to decompose the quantum geometric tensor, we isolate the constraint imposed by the uniform parent curvature and show that the excess quantum weight above the bound equals twice the weaker circular transition weight. For a noninteracting parabolic band with a periodic scalar potential, Landau-level mixing preserves the integrated relative curvature while the occupied direct gap remains open. Nevertheless, uncorrected sub-cyclotron absorption need not satisfy the projected bound. Using exact circular-dipole relations, we reconstruct the low-frequency guiding-centre weight and signed dichroism from circularly polarized absorption. This reconstruction removes the first-order orbit-polarization contribution. For an insulating filling of an isolated lowest-Landau-level-derived cluster, a potential-gradient estimate bounds the omitted remote-transition weight quadratically at weak coupling. candidates.title: Electronic Wichmann-Kroll correction to the energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms
candidates.abstract: Using modern multiloop calculation methods, we obtain correction to energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms due to the leading-order ($\proptoα(Zα)^3$) Wichmann-Kroll electronic potential. Our result is expressed in terms of generalized polylogarithms. As a byproduct, we also obtain the Wichmann-Kroll potential in momentum space in terms of the same functions.

candidates.title: Composite Dielectric-Loaded Metallic Metagratings for Dual-Polarized Transmissive Beam Manipulation
candidates.abstract: We present and experimentally demonstrate a comprehensive analytical suite for the design of transmissive metal-based metagratings (MGs) for dual-polarized anomalous refraction. Considering a composite configuration of perforated metallic slabs with controlled dielectric loading, we develop a rigorous mode-matching formulation tying the various MG degrees of freedom to the various reflected and transmitted Floquet-Bloch modes, enabling efficient beam deflection for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations. Inherently versatile, the analytical framework accurately models single-layer and double-layer constructs with multiple rectangular perforations per unit cell, each potentially loaded with dielectric material. We harness this degree-of-freedom abundance to devise diverse polarization-sensitive transmissive MGs, ranging from all-metallic single-layer and double-layer structures for single-polarized (TM or TE) perfect anomalous refraction, to dielectric-loaded architectures implementing dual-polarized routing of the incident wave. candidates.title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
candidates.abstract: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $η$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. candidates.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
candidates.abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. candidates.title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
candidates.abstract: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.

candidates.title: Features investigated: A detailed study of axion monodromy inflation using CLiENT
candidates.abstract: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency $ω\simeq 51$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at $ω\simeq 31$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant.
